title: 20.11 A Crystal-Less BodyID with an Asynchronous Clockless Leakage-Powered Wake-Up Receiver and Over-the-Channel Clock Recovery
problem: Wake-up receivers for ultra-low-power wearables traditionally require always-running clocks and external crystal oscillators for sampling and correlation, consuming unnecessary idle power, adding size/cost, and requiring ULP oscillator with external calibration reference.
motivation: Battery-less and ultra-low-power wearables and implants demand sub-microsecond wake-up latency without external references or always-on clocks.
method: Asynchronous clockless wake-up receiver design leveraging over-the-channel clock recovery from incoming RF signal to enable direct digital correlation without always-running oscillator, powered by device leakage during idle state, eliminating need for external crystal reference.
key_novelty: Clockless asynchronous design using in-band clock recovery to eliminate crystal oscillator and always-running clock, enabling full battery-less operation at leakage power levels.
contributions: Leakage-powered operation during idle (sub-μW regime) without external crystal or always-running oscillator
Over-the-channel clock recovery enabling asynchronous reception without local oscillator calibration
Sub-latency wake-up capability (latency specifications not stated but implied <<2ms) for battery-less nodes
limitations: Specific wake-up latency, range, and sensitivity metrics not provided; scalability to other wearable protocols not discussed.
